issues.label: Equipment Breakdown
issues.summary: Critical machinery failure during peak field operations causing harvest delays, crop losses, and cascading scheduling disruptions across the operation

circuits.detail: Primary tractor power units offline due to mechanical or hydraulic system failure
Combine threshing or separation systems failing during narrow harvest windows
Preventive maintenance programs insufficient to prevent in-season breakdowns
Critical replacement parts unavailable from dealer inventory or supply chain
Telematic diagnostic alerts unheeded or misinterpreted before catastrophic failure

issues.label: Precision Technology Failure
issues.summary: GPS guidance, variable-rate controllers, or telematics systems malfunctioning causing misapplication, overlap, skips, and wasted inputs

circuits.detail: GPS signal loss or RTK correction failure degrading auto-steer accuracy to unacceptable levels
Telematics data transmission failing, eliminating remote monitoring and diagnostic capability
Planter section control malfunctions causing double-planting or skipped rows
Sprayer rate controllers misapplying chemicals at incorrect concentrations
Tractor implement bus communication errors disrupting ISOBUS-controlled operations

issues.label: Capital Overextension
issues.summary: Excessive equipment investment relative to farm revenue creating unsustainable debt loads, deferred maintenance, and financial stress

circuits.detail: Equipment financing commitments exceeding cash flow capacity and debt service coverage ratios
Fleet overcapacity with underutilized power units depreciating faster than they generate returns
Maintenance budgets cut to service equipment debt, accelerating wear and breakdown risk
Parts inventory depleted to reduce carrying costs, increasing downtime during breakdowns
Aging combine fleet retained past economic life due to inability to finance replacements

issues.label: Operator Shortage

circuits.detail: Tractor seats unfilled during peak demand, leaving field-ready equipment idle
Combine operation requiring specialized skill set unavailable in local labor market
Precision technology complexity exceeding available operator training and competency
Tillage operations delayed as limited operators prioritize planting and harvest tasks
Planting windows missed due to insufficient operators to run all available planter units

issues.label: Parts Supply Chain Disruption

circuits.detail: Parts distribution channels unable to fulfill orders for critical wear and breakdown components
